tours.name: Credit Sales Order
tours.description: Step-by-step guide to selling to a credit customer on 14 Days payment terms: create the quotation, set the payment type to Credit and the payment terms to 14 Days, confirm it, deliver the goods and invoice the customer. Before you start: you need access to the Sales app and an existing credit customer who has no overdue invoices (this guide uses DIDULA MOTORES). The customer pays after the due date, so no payment is registered in this guide. In every screenshot the red box shows exactly what to click or fill in.

description_i18n.en_US: Step-by-step guide to selling to a credit customer on 14 Days payment terms: create the quotation, set the payment type to Credit and the payment terms to 14 Days, confirm it, deliver the goods and invoice the customer. Before you start: you need access to the Sales app and an existing credit customer who has no overdue invoices (this guide uses DIDULA MOTORES). The customer pays after the due date, so no payment is registered in this guide. In every screenshot the red box shows exactly what to click or fill in.

steps.title: Open the Sales app from the Odoo home screen to start a new sale

steps.content: Log in to Odoo. On the home screen you will see a grid of app icons. Find the **Sales** icon (red box) and click it. The Sales app opens and its menu appears across the top of the screen.

steps.title: Click the Customer field and type the credit customer name to search for them

steps.description: Why: Odoo needs a customer to price the order and to print the invoice. Watch out: for a credit sale choose a customer who is set up for credit and has no overdue invoices. A customer with overdue invoices is held back by the credit limit check and needs extra approvals, so pick another customer.

description_i18n.en_US: Why: this tells Odoo the customer will pay after the due date, not at once. Credit orders are checked against the customer credit limit. Check: the field shows "Credit".

steps.content: When you selected the customer, Odoo filled in the **Payment Terms** from that customer record. Click the **Payment Terms** field (red box) to open the list of payment terms.

steps.description: Why: these values decide when the invoice is due. Check: no credit limit warning is shown. Watch out: if Odoo shows a credit limit warning or a **Request Credit Limit Approval** button, the customer is over the limit or overdue; choose another customer.

description_i18n.en_US: Why: these values decide when the invoice is due. Check: no credit limit warning is shown. Watch out: if Odoo shows a credit limit warning or a **Request Credit Limit Approval** button, the customer is over the limit or overdue; choose another customer.

steps.title: Click Confirm to turn the quotation into a Sales Order

title_i18n.en_US: Click Confirm to turn the quotation into a Sales Order

steps.content: At the top of the form, click the purple **Confirm** button (red box). Odoo saves the quotation and turns it into a confirmed Sales Order.

content_i18n.en_US: At the top of the form, click the purple **Confirm** button (red box). Odoo saves the quotation and turns it into a confirmed Sales Order.

steps.description: Why: confirming makes the order official and creates the delivery that you will process next. Check: the status bar moves to "Sales Order", the number changes to S0..., and a **Delivery** button appears at the top.

description_i18n.en_US: Why: confirming makes the order official and creates the delivery that you will process next. Check: the status bar moves to "Sales Order", the number changes to S0..., and a **Delivery** button appears at the top.

steps.title: Click the Delivery button to open the delivery

content_i18n.en_US: At the top of the order, click the **Delivery** smart button (red box). The delivery transfer opens, for example JM-EK/OUT/01060.

steps.description: Why: the delivery is the document your warehouse uses to hand the goods to the customer. Check: you see the delivery with the product line.

description_i18n.en_US: Why: the delivery is the document your warehouse uses to hand the goods to the customer. Check: you see the delivery with the product line.

steps.title: Click Validate to deliver the goods

content_i18n.en_US: Click the purple **Validate** button at the top left (red box). If Odoo asks a question, confirm it.

steps.description: Why: this hands the goods to the customer and takes them out of stock. Check: the status bar at the top right moves to **Done**. Watch out: if the product is not in stock, Odoo cannot reserve it, so check the stock first.

description_i18n.en_US: Why: this hands the goods to the customer and takes them out of stock. Check: the status bar at the top right moves to **Done**. Watch out: if the product is not in stock, Odoo cannot reserve it, so check the stock first.

content_i18n.en_US: The delivery is now **Done**. At the top left, click the sales order number (red box, for example S02729) to go back to the order.

steps.description: Check: the order opens again and now shows a **Create Invoice** button.

steps.content: Click **Create Invoice** (red box). If a small window asks which kind of invoice to create, keep the default "Regular invoice" and click **Create Draft Invoice**.

steps.description: Why: the invoice is the document you give the customer to ask for payment. Check: a draft invoice opens with the customer, the product and the amount.

description_i18n.en_US: Why: the invoice is the document you give the customer to ask for payment. Check: a draft invoice opens with the customer, the product and the amount.

steps.title: Click Confirm to post the invoice

title_i18n.en_US: Click Confirm to post the invoice

steps.content: On the draft invoice, click **Confirm** (red box). The invoice gets its final number, for example FTI/2026/00602.

content_i18n.en_US: On the draft invoice, click **Confirm** (red box). The invoice gets its final number, for example FTI/2026/00602.

steps.description: Why: a draft invoice has no accounting effect; confirming it records the sale in the books. Check: the status bar moves to **Posted**. Watch out: for a credit sale you do not register a payment now; the customer pays later.

description_i18n.en_US: Why: a draft invoice has no accounting effect; confirming it records the sale in the books. Check: the status bar moves to **Posted**. Watch out: for a credit sale you do not register a payment now; the customer pays later.

steps.title: Check the 14 Days due date on the invoice

title_i18n.en_US: Check the 14 Days due date on the invoice

steps.content: On the posted invoice, look at the **Due Date** (red box). It is **14 days after the Invoice Date**, because the order used the 14 Days payment term.

content_i18n.en_US: On the posted invoice, look at the **Due Date** (red box). It is **14 days after the Invoice Date**, because the order used the 14 Days payment term.

steps.description: Result: product delivered, customer invoiced on credit, due in 14 days. Check: Due Date = Invoice Date + 14 days, the Amount Due equals the Total, and no payment ribbon is shown.

description_i18n.en_US: Result: product delivered, customer invoiced on credit, due in 14 days. Check: Due Date = Invoice Date + 14 days, the Amount Due equals the Total, and no payment ribbon is shown.
